question: How do visually impaired (blind) people read books using the Braille system? 📖
explanation: Awesome! Braille uses special raised dots on paper, and people read them by feeling the dots with their fingers! 👆
hint: They use their fingertips.

question: Who invented this amazing reading system? 💡
explanation: Great job! Louis Braille was a very smart person who invented this helpful system! 👨‍🦯
hint: The system is named after him.

question: What is the shape of Braille letters? 🔵
explanation: Super! Braille letters are made of small raised dots that pop up from the paper! 🔵
hint: They look like little bumps.

question: Which body part is used to read Braille? 🖐️
explanation: Wonderful! We use the sensitive tips of our fingers to feel the tiny dots! 👆
hint: They are at the end of your hands.

question: What kind of paper is used to write Braille? 📄
explanation: Excellent! Thick paper is used so the raised dots stay bumpy and do not get flat! 🗂️
hint: It is strong and heavy.

question: How do the Braille dots feel when you touch them? ✨
explanation: Spot on! The dots pop up from the paper, so they feel bumpy under your fingers! ✨
hint: Like tiny little hills.

question: How many dots make up one Braille cell? 🔢
explanation: Awesome! A Braille cell is made of six dots, just like the number six on a dice! 🎲
hint: Three on the left, three on the right.

question: What do different combinations of dots make? 🔤
explanation: Great job! By changing which dots are raised, we can make every letter of the alphabet! 🔤
hint: A, B, C, D...

question: What tool is used to punch the holes in Braille paper? 🖊️
explanation: Super! A stylus is a special pointed tool used to press the dots into the paper! 🖊️
hint: It looks a bit like a pen.

question: What frame holds the paper still while writing Braille? 🔲
explanation: Fantastic! A slate is a metal or plastic frame that keeps the paper perfectly straight! 🔲
hint: It starts with the letter S.

question: In which direction do we read Braille? ➡️
explanation: Wonderful! Just like regular English books, Braille is read from left to right! ➡️
hint: It goes the same way we read.

question: Can visually impaired children read storybooks? 📚
explanation: Excellent! Thanks to Braille, children who cannot see can read all their favorite stories! 📖
hint: They use their fingers to read.

question: What do we call people who cannot see? 🕶️
explanation: Awesome! People who cannot see or have very low vision are called visually impaired. 🕶️
hint: It means their eyes do not work well.

question: Can we write numbers using Braille? 🔢
explanation: Great job! Braille has special dot patterns for numbers like 1, 2, and 3 too! 🔢
hint: Math is possible in Braille!

question: How should we treat our visually impaired friends? 🤝
explanation: Super! We should always be kind, helpful, and friendly to everyone! 🤝
hint: We should be good friends.

question: What stick do many visually impaired people use to walk safely? 🦯
explanation: Fantastic! A white cane helps them feel the ground and walk safely everywhere! 🦯
hint: It is a long white stick.

question: Which animal is specially trained to help guide blind people? 🦮
explanation: Wonderful! Guide dogs are smart and helpful friends that lead people safely! 🦮
hint: It says 'Woof!'

question: What is another fun way to enjoy stories if you cannot see the book? 🎧
explanation: Excellent! Audiobooks let you listen to stories being read out loud! 🎧
hint: You use your ears for this.

question: Why did Louis Braille want to invent this system? 🏫
explanation: Awesome! Louis loved learning and wanted a way for everyone to read books easily! 📖
hint: He wanted to study and learn.

question: What sense is used the most when reading Braille? 🖐️
explanation: Great job! The sense of touch helps our fingers feel the bumpy dots! 🖐️
hint: We use our skin for this.

question: When do we celebrate World Braille Day? 🗓️
explanation: Super! We celebrate World Braille Day on January 4th, which is Louis Braille's birthday! 🗓️
hint: It is early in the new year.

question: How did Louis Braille act when he lost his sight? 🦸
explanation: Fantastic! Louis was very brave and worked hard to invent something amazing! 🦸
hint: He was strong and smart.

question: What do we do to the paper after punching holes with a stylus? 📄
explanation: Wonderful! We push dots down from the back, so we flip the paper over to feel the bumps! 🔄
hint: We turn it around.

question: What does a stylus look like? 🖊️
explanation: Excellent! A stylus is small and pointed, just like a pen without ink! 🖊️
hint: You hold it in your hand to write.

question: Can blind children play games? 🎲
explanation: Awesome! Blind children can play lots of fun games, especially toys with textures! 🎲
hint: Everyone loves to play!

question: Are there special bumpy toys for blind children? 🧸
explanation: Great job! Bumpy toys and puzzles help visually impaired children have lots of fun! 🧸
hint: They use their hands to play.

question: What should you do if a visually impaired person needs to cross the road? 🚦
explanation: Super! Always politely ask if they need help crossing the street safely! 🚦
hint: Be a helpful friend.

question: How should we talk to a visually impaired friend? 🗣️
explanation: Fantastic! Speaking clearly helps them know who you are and what you are saying! 🗣️
hint: Use your normal, friendly voice.

question: What is the best way to learn Braille? ⏳
explanation: Wonderful! Just like learning anything new, Braille takes practice and patience! ⏳
hint: You have to try it many times.

question: Braille helps visually impaired people to become... 🌟
explanation: Excellent! Reading Braille helps them learn, work, and do things on their own! 🌟
hint: Doing things by themselves.

question: Which country was Louis Braille from? 🇫🇷
explanation: Awesome! Louis Braille was born in a beautiful country called France! 🇫🇷
hint: It is in Europe.

question: How do you make a Braille dot on paper? 🕳️
explanation: Great job! You gently push the stylus into the thick paper to make a tiny bump! 🖊️
hint: You press down.

question: Can Braille be used for languages other than English? 🌍
explanation: Super! Braille is an amazing code that can be used to write almost any language in the world! 🌍
hint: It works all over the globe.

question: Why is it important to learn to read? 🧠
explanation: Fantastic! Reading helps everyone learn new things and grow a very smart brain! 🧠
hint: It fills your mind with ideas.

question: Where do visually impaired children learn Braille? 🏫
explanation: Wonderful! Teachers at school help children practice and learn the Braille alphabet! 🏫
hint: It is a place of learning.

question: How do you know it is your friend if you cannot see them? 👂
explanation: Excellent! Every person has a special voice that helps friends know who is speaking! 🗣️
hint: You hear it with your ears.

question: What is the best thing to say when you meet a blind friend? 👋
explanation: Awesome! Saying 'hello' and telling them your name is the nicest way to say hi! 👋
hint: It is a friendly greeting.

question: If you see a Braille book, you should... 📖
explanation: Great job! Braille books are very special, so we must be gentle so we don't flatten the dots! 📖
hint: Be gentle with it.

question: What part of the stylus touches the paper? 📌
explanation: Super! The small pointed end presses into the paper to make the neat little dots! 📌
hint: It is the sharp part.

question: What happens if Braille paper is too thin? 📄
explanation: Fantastic! Thin paper rips easily when poked, so Braille needs thick, strong paper! 📄
hint: It gets a hole in it.

question: How does reading Braille make visually impaired people feel? 😊
explanation: Wonderful! Reading opens up magical worlds and makes everyone feel happy and smart! 😊
hint: It is a good feeling.

question: Are elevators sometimes labeled with Braille? 🛗
explanation: Excellent! Many elevators have Braille on the buttons to help people find the right floor! 🛗
hint: Look near the buttons!

question: Can you find Braille on medicine boxes? 💊
explanation: Awesome! Medicine boxes often have Braille so blind people know exactly what medicine it is! 💊
hint: It helps keep people safe.

question: What did Louis Braille use before he invented his dot system? 🔤
explanation: Great job! Before Braille, people tried to make huge wooden letters, but they were too hard to read! 🔤
hint: Giant alphabet shapes.

question: Why are dots better than big raised letters? 🖐️
explanation: Super! Your fingertip can feel a small dot pattern much faster than tracing a giant letter! 🖐️
hint: It saves a lot of time.

question: A group of six Braille dots looks like a small... 🟦
explanation: Fantastic! The six dots are arranged in a neat little rectangle shape! 🟦
hint: It has four straight sides.

question: What is the best way to practice reading Braille? 📖
explanation: Wonderful! Practicing a little bit every day makes your fingers super fast at reading! 📖
hint: Do it daily.

question: How did Louis Braille change the world? 🌍
explanation: Excellent! His brilliant invention has helped millions of blind people read and write! 🌍
hint: He did something amazing for people.

question: Who can learn the Braille alphabet? 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
explanation: Awesome! Anyone, whether they can see or not, can learn the amazing Braille code! 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
hint: All of us can try it!

question: Braille is a very special... 🗝️
explanation: Great job! It is like a brilliant code made of dots that unlocks the magic of reading! 🗝️
hint: It has patterns to figure out.
